usageNotes: Use this to audit what privileges a specific user or API token actually has in effect across the cluster — useful for troubleshooting access denials or verifying least-privilege configurations. Omitting both `userid` and `path` returns the full privilege tree for the currently authenticated caller. To inspect another user's permissions, your token or user must hold `Sys.Audit` on `/access`; without it, you can only query yourself or tokens you own.

examples.summary: Fetch all effective permissions for a specific API token scoped to a single path

tips: Omit `path` to get the full permission tree; supply it to narrow the response to one ACL path (faster for targeted checks).
The response maps each path to a privilege object where values are booleans indicating whether the privilege propagates to children.
API tokens always have permissions that are the intersection of their owner's permissions and any explicit token ACLs — effective permissions may be narrower than the owner's.
This endpoint is safe to call frequently; it is read-only and does not alter any cluster state.
